comps._note: How finished homes are valued. New builds use new-construction sales only; rehab uses existing-home sales matched on size and age. Older-home sales are never the value of a new build: when new-construction sales are too few, they are shown only as a labeled floor.

newConstruction.rule: Valid arm's-length sales in the last 3 years of homes built no more than 10 years before the sale year, at least 600 sq ft of living area and $20,000, within ±40% of the planned home's size when enough. Same City neighborhood (or municipality) when it has at least 5 such sales, otherwise areas of the same market tier (never a richer market), nearest first; widen from ¼ mile to 3 miles until 8, keep the nearest 12; drop sales beyond 1.5× the middle-half spread of $/SF; at least 5 needed.

selection._note: How the new-construction comp set is chosen (deterministic). 1) Same City neighborhood (or same municipality outside the City) when it has at least sameAreaMinComps sales; otherwise the nearest sales by distance. 2) Widen by radius until nearestMin sales, then keep the nearest nearestMax. 3) Drop sales whose $/SF is beyond outlierIqrMultiplier x IQR from the quartiles (listed in the receipt). Editable assumptions.
selection.tierNote: Market-tier matching (appraisal-style, never demographic): when the subject's own area has fewer than sameAreaMinComps new-construction sales, candidate comps must come from areas whose market tier (median $/SF of existing-home sales, engine/config/area-market-tiers.json; 5 years when 3 have too few sales) is no higher than the subject area's tier and at most tierBand below it (never a richer market). An area with no tier borrows the median tier of its tierNeighbors nearest tiered areas. Too few sales in the band: any area priced no higher than the subject area's tier (never a richer market). Still too few: no new-home value (older-home sales shown as a floor); comps are never pulled from richer markets by distance alone. Comps are kept within ±sizeBand of the planned home's finished size when that leaves enough sales.

existingMatch.rule: After-repair value: nearby valid sales of the same use in Good or better condition (county assessment condition), kept when living area is within 35% of the building; at least 5, otherwise all Good-or-better sales nearby with a note. As-is sales of older homes are not used as the value after a rehab.
